This page follows `convert.R` from top to bottom.
The code is shown in small parts.
The output comes from the example data.

The full script is at the bottom.
Run it from the project folder:

```bash
Rscript convert.R
```

## 1. Settings

The top of the script holds the names and numbers.
There is no config file.
Change these values for a new survey.

```r
BASE_DIR <- getwd()
INPUT_DIR <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "data")
OUTPUT_DIR <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "output")

# Enter the names of the people who recorded each field group.
# Use a pipe (|) between names when a group has more than one recorder.
RECORDED_BY <- c(
  Group_1 = paste(
    "Hannah Heutz", "Biel Masnou Domènech", "Valéria Prando",
    "Ana Soler-Fajardo", "Teresa Madurell", sep = " | "
  ),
  Group_2 = paste(
    "Albert Martinez", "Marco Simoes", "Aghogho Kolawole-Daniels",
    "Eunice Opeyemi Idowu", "Hector Serrano Cereijo", sep = " | "
  ),
  Group_3 = paste(
    "Martha Vounatsi", "Nhanque Filipe", "Abigail Mwalimu",
    "Sébastien Lhoumeau", "Mayday Haulofu", "Ahmed Harat", sep = " | "
  ),
  Group_4 = paste(
    "Monika Szynaka", "Pilar Pérez Abellán", "Alfonso Ferreira Sarracino",
    "Nestor Echedey Bosch Guerra", sep = " | "
  )
)

PROJECT_CODE <- "MBON-P2P"
COUNTRY_CODE <- "PT"        # ISO 3166-1 alpha-2
COUNTRY_ID_CODE <- "PRT"    # ISO 3166-1 alpha-3, used in the identifiers
LOCALITY <- "Forte do Negrito"
POINTS_PER_IMAGE <- 100

# The metadata uses the short name "TG-7".
CAMERA <- "OM System Tough TG-7"

# Photo events use a 1 m position uncertainty.
COORDINATE_UNCERTAINTY_M <- 1
```

Photo events use 1 metre position uncertainty.
The georeference protocol says the GPS is built into the camera.
The sampling protocol cites the MBON protocol and its two reference links.

Each occurrence uses the string for its photo's group:

```{r}
#| echo: false
events <- read.csv("output/event.csv", colClasses = "character",
                   check.names = FALSE)
first_occurrences <- read.csv(
  "output/occurrence.csv", colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE
)
cat("survey ID:        ", events$eventID[1], "\n")
cat("first photo ID:   ", events$eventID[2], "\n")
cat("photos:           ", nrow(events) - 1, "\n")
cat("first recordedBy: ", first_occurrences$recordedBy[1], "\n")
cat("first identifiedBy:", first_occurrences$identifiedBy[1], "\n")
```

## 2. The TAXA table

Each label that becomes an occurrence has one entry.
The entry has the CoralNet label ID, the scientific name, the AphiaID, and the taxonomy.

```r
TAXA <- list(
  CHLOROPHY = list(
    label_id = "4095", name = "Chlorophyta", aphia = "801",
    authorship = "Pascher, 1914", rank = "phylum",
    kingdom = "Plantae", phylum = "Chlorophyta",
    class = "", order = "", family = "", genus = ""
  ),
  CIRRIPE = list(
    label_id = "2812", name = "Chthamalus stellatus",
    aphia = "106231", authorship = "(Poli, 1791)", rank = "species",
    kingdom = "Animalia", phylum = "Arthropoda",
    class = "Thecostraca", order = "Balanomorpha",
    family = "Chthamalidae", genus = "Chthamalus"
  ),
  # ... eight more taxa ...
)
```

This is the result for the example:

```{r}
#| echo: false
occurrences <- read.csv("output/occurrence.csv", colClasses = "character",
                        check.names = FALSE)
taxa_counts <- as.data.frame(table(occurrences$scientificName))
names(taxa_counts) <- c("scientificName", "occurrences")
print(taxa_counts, row.names = FALSE)
```

## 3. Read the files

The script uses only base R.
There are no extra R packages.

```r
read_table <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
           stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
}
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
metadata <- read.csv("data/metadata.csv", colClasses = "character",
                     check.names = FALSE)
annotations <- read.csv("data/annotations.csv", colClasses = "character",
                        check.names = FALSE)
cat(nrow(metadata), "images\n")
cat(nrow(annotations), "points\n\n")
for (i in 1:3) {
  cat(metadata$Name[i], metadata$Date[i], "\n")
}
cat("\nfirst position:", metadata$Latitude[1], metadata$Longitude[1], "\n")
```

## 4. Make the events

The parent event is the whole survey.
Each photo gets a child event.
The photo event ID ends with the frame number.

```r
survey_id <- function(date) {
  paste(
    PROJECT_CODE, gsub("-", "", date), COUNTRY_ID_CODE, ISLAND_CODE,
    SITE_CODE, STRATA, sep = ":"
  )
}

group_code <- function(group) {
  gsub("Group_", "G", group, fixed = TRUE)
}

frame_from_name <- function(image_name) {
  stem <- sub("\\.[^.]*$", "", image_name)
  frame <- substr(stem, nchar(stem) - 3, nchar(stem))
  if (!grepl("^[0-9]{4}$", frame)) {
    stop("Cannot find a 4-digit frame number in ", image_name)
  }
  frame
}
```

The child event ID also includes the group, because the same frame number can
appear in more than one group.

```{r}
#| echo: false
cat("parent:\n")
cat(" ", events$eventID[1], "\n")
cat("  ", events$decimalLatitude[1], events$decimalLongitude[1], "\n\n")
cat("first child:\n")
cat(" ", events$eventID[2], "\n")
cat("  ", events$decimalLatitude[2], events$decimalLongitude[2], "\n")
cat("  parent:", events$parentEventID[2], "\n")
```

## 5. Count the points

The script groups the points by image and label.
It counts all points.
It also finds the points made by CoralNet's automated classifier, which is stored as `robot`.

```r
# Inside the loop for one image and one label:
points <- annotations[
  annotations$Name == image & annotations[["Label code"]] == code, ,
  drop = FALSE
]
count <- nrow(points)
machine <- sum(points$Annotator == "robot")
human <- count - machine
annotators <- ifelse(
  points$Annotator == "robot",
  "CoralNet machine learning annotator",
  points$Annotator
)
annotators <- sort(unique(annotators), method = "radix")
```

The `robot` value is written as `CoralNet machine learning annotator` in `identifiedBy`.
Human usernames are kept as they are.
When a row has more than one value, the values are separated by `|`.

The percent cover is points divided by total points, times 100.

```{r}
#| echo: false
cat(sprintf("%-24s %6s  %-18s %s\n",
            "taxon", "cover", "basis", "identifiedBy"))
cat(strrep("-", 80), "\n")
for (i in 1:8) {
  cat(sprintf("%-24s %6s  %-18s %s\n",
              occurrences$scientificName[i],
              occurrences$organismQuantity[i],
              occurrences$basisOfRecord[i],
              occurrences$identifiedBy[i]))
}
```

## 6. Make the measurements

A measurement is one number with a type and a unit.
This helper keeps the rows short.

```r
measurement <- function(event_id, occurrence_id, name, mtype, value, unit,
                        unit_id = "", type_id = "", method = "",
                        remarks = "") {
  prefix <- if (nzchar(occurrence_id)) occurrence_id else event_id
  list(
    eventID = event_id,
    occurrenceID = occurrence_id,
    measurementID = paste0(prefix, ":", name),
    measurementType = mtype,
    measurementTypeID = type_id,
    measurementValue = value,
    measurementUnit = unit,
    measurementUnitID = unit_id,
    measurementMethod = method,
    measurementRemarks = remarks
  )
}
```

The first measurements in the file are:

```{r}
#| echo: false
measurements <- read.csv(
  "output/extendedmeasurementorfact.csv",
  colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE
)
for (i in 1:5) {
  cat(sprintf("%-42s %8s %s\n",
              measurements$measurementType[i],
              measurements$measurementValue[i],
              measurements$measurementUnit[i]))
}
```

## 7. Write the files

The script writes three CSV files.
Then it writes `meta.xml`.
Then it puts everything in a zip file.

```r
make_zip <- function() {
  old_dir <- setwd(OUTPUT_DIR)
  on.exit(setwd(old_dir), add = TRUE)
  unlink("p2p-azores-2026.zip")
  utils::zip(
    "p2p-azores-2026.zip",
    files = c(
      "event.csv", "occurrence.csv", "extendedmeasurementorfact.csv",
      "meta.xml", "README.txt"
    ),
    flags = "-j"
  )
  "p2p-azores-2026.zip"
}
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
files <- c(
  "event.csv", "occurrence.csv", "extendedmeasurementorfact.csv",
  "meta.xml", "README.txt", "p2p-azores-2026.zip"
)
cat("output files:\n")
for (name in files) {
  size <- file.info(file.path("output", name))$size
  cat(sprintf("  %-36s %8d bytes\n", name, size))
}
cat("\nzip contents:\n")
for (name in unzip("output/p2p-azores-2026.zip", list = TRUE)$Name) {
  cat(" ", name, "\n")
}
```
